title: Where the Mind Goes
logline: Newcomers arrive at a forest meditation centre and try to sit still, and on the first evening a teacher asks each of them one question: where does your mind go?
human_question: Why do we each lose our way differently, and what brings each of us back?

situation.what_happens: A centre that takes lay newcomers admits a handful of people for their first retreat. They sit, fidget, walk, sleep, and discover within hours how little of their attention they command. A teacher who cannot read anyone's mind does what the sources describe: asks each person what comes easily and where the mind runs, then gives a practice that fits. Over a few days something small shifts, or nothing does.
situation.who_is_involved: First-time lay meditators; a teacher whose whole job is to fit a practice to a person; and the community of the centre, whose rules and rhythm hold the days together.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For a newcomer, whether any of this is for them, and what they find out about their own mind in the meantime. For the teacher, the risk of giving the wrong practice to the wrong person. For the centre, its quiet, which visitors and cameras both disturb.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins with arrival and noise in the head, and turns on the first conversation. Days pass with very little visible happening. It ends with people leaving, slightly changed or not at all, and nobody can say in advance which. Reality decides, and nothing here can be arranged.

concept_merge.why_together: C086 says the many meditation subjects exist because people differ, and describes a teacher who cannot read minds asking the student which states are frequent and which subject comes easily, then giving a fitting practice [C086-P4:L278; C086-M:L5]. C008 supplies what the newcomer is actually meeting: restlessness as the loss of the power to stay with one object, which scatters the rest of the mind with it [C008-P:L62]. One is the difficulty, the other is how it is met person by person.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the answer to being scattered is not a single method but a particular one, chosen after someone has looked or asked. C086 alone becomes a typology; C008 alone becomes a complaint about attention.

concept_links.why: The digest carries this as one of its own story seeds and describes exactly this conversation: a teacher who cannot read minds asks which states are frequent and which subject feels easy, then gives a practice that fits [C086-P4:L278], and the whole point of the many subjects is to fit the person [C086-M:L5]. Its warnings apply directly: this is not a personality test and the teacher's advice may never be presented as a diagnosis.

The digest describes restlessness as the loss of one-pointedness, which sends the whole mind astray [C008-P:L62]. A first retreat is where people meet that directly and describe it in their own words, which is the only form in which the film should carry it.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The many practices exist because people differ; a good guide does not hand everyone the same instruction but looks closely, or simply asks. Whatever scatters your attention, meeting it starts with someone finding out what yours actually does.
what_must_be_real: The centre, the newcomers and every word they say. No one performs meditation for the camera, the teacher's advice is never presented as a diagnosis, and the centre's rules come before the film.
position_hint: middle, if ever used on its own: wherever a group needs the moment when being lost stops being general and is met one person at a time.
risks: Disrupting a retreat; the centre's rules come first.
Turning a person's inner struggle into spectacle or into a lesson.
Temperament presented as a personality test.
Reading a newcomer's difficulty as a statement about the kind of person they are, which is the reading the C049 digest forbids.
drop_if: The centre does not allow the filming of newcomers or of a teacher's conversation.

connections.note: Its guide who asks rather than assumes, and the learner's own account of where attention goes, now live inside the workshop film.
Leanings seen in a family's shared work, then met one by one by someone teaching.

selection.reason: Folded into IDEA-0060, which gains the guide who asks rather than assumes and the learner's own account of where attention goes.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
